test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If two pipes A and B function simultaneously, an empty tank will be filled in 20 hours. If pipe A, working alone, fills this empty tank 9 hours faster than pipe B can fill it working alone, then how many hours does it take pipe B to fill this empty tank while working alone?
solution:
Given:

Two pipes A and B working simultaneously can fill a tank in 20 hours.

The pipe A fills the tank 9 hours faster than the other.

Calculation:

Let the slower pipe B can fill the tank in x hours,

Then faster pipe A can fill the tank in (x – 9) hours.

Tank filled by slower pipe B in 1 hour = 1/x

Tank filled by faster pipe A in 1 hour = 1/(x – 9)

Part filled by both the pipes A and B in 1 hour = 1/20

According to the question

1/x + 1/(x – 9) = 1/20

⇒ [(x – 9) + x]/x(x – 9) = 1/20

⇒ 20(x – 9) + 20x = x(x – 9)

⇒ 20x – 180 + 20x = x² – 9x

⇒ x² – 49x + 180 = 0

⇒ x² – 45x – 4x + 180 = 0

⇒ x(x – 45) – 4(x – 45) = 0

⇒ (x – 45)(x – 4) = 0

⇒ x = 45, 4

But x = 4 is not possible since (x – 9) i.e. (4 – 9) will give a negative value

Hence slower pipe B can fill the tank in 45 hours

∴ The pipe B alone takes 45 hours to fill the tank.
